newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-JORDAN HOPING TO CELEBRATE HIS TEAM'S 100TH RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-JORDAN HOPING TO CELEBRATE HIS TEAM'S 100TH RACE.

text.p: Team boss Eddie Jordan said on Saturday that he had ended his long feud with double world champion Michael Schumacher on the eve of the Jordan team's 100th grand prix.
Jordan, who gave Schumacher his debut in 1991 but lost his services to Benetton after only one race, had not spoken to the German driver for nearly five years until late last year.
"But we are talking again now and it is nice," he admitted after revealing that the two had settled out of court to end their long-running row over what Jordan always felt was a broken agreement.
"It was an honourable decision for both parties to take," said Jordan. "Michael and I came to a very amicable understanding about the differences and over the pain that there was at the time.
"We cannot hide the fact that I was really upset about it. But I was perhaps a little bit naive at that stage. It was our first year and we were struggling to stay alive financially.
Jordan is understood to have received a settlement of more than $1 million to end the feud.
As part of the agreement, he also went on to sign Michael Schumacher's younger brother Ralf, 21, for this season's championship.
Ralf Schumacher, fast and determined, has been a revelation already this year but is still searching for his and the team's first points in Sunday's 72-lap race.
"This has to be the start of a new era for the team," said Jordan. "We have grown up now. At the start we were just fighting to survive and it was difficult for us.
"Now we have to start winning and to join the teams at the highest echelon of our sport."
